author: reek
body: The unary process-exit means something on bare metal. A child that calls process-exit N and a child that returns N both leave N in the slot's exit-status cell -- the unary helper stores its argument, and __proc_entry stores the closure's return value before joining the exit path. The exit wake loop delivers the status into a blocked waiter's saved RAX, and process-wait's already-dead path reads the cell directly, so process-wait answers the child's status whichever side of the exit race the waiter lands on. The two children use different constants so a wait that answers the wrong child's status, or a stale zero, cannot pass.
